# FIN-210 Travel and expense (rev. 2026-07-01)

1. Book air and hotels through Corporate Travel Partners (corwin@ctptravel.com). Economy class.
2. Lodging is capped at the GSA per diem lodging rate for the city (before taxes). An exception needs the
   traveler's supervisor's approval in writing before booking; nobody approves their own exception.
3. Meals: GSA M&IE for the city; 75% on the first and last day of travel; deduct meals provided (breakfast $20,
   lunch $22, dinner $33 at the $80 rate).
4. Personal car: the IRS standard mileage rate in effect on the date of travel (76 cents a mile from July 1,
   2026). Round trip from the office or home, whichever is shorter.
5. Submit expense reports in Concur within 30 days with receipts for lodging and anything over $75.
6. Cancel unneeded hotel rooms before the hotel's deadline; no-show charges are not reimbursed.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# FIN-120 Purchasing and P-card

- P-card: single purchases up to $500. Splitting a purchase to stay under the limit is prohibited.
- Over $500: a purchase request approved by the office manager (Carol Mendes), then a PO.
- Vendor invoices: match to the PO and the delivery or service record; code to the project or overhead; the
  budget owner approves; AP pays. Query differences with the vendor before approving.
- Vendor bank or payment changes: only HQ Accounts Payable may change them, after calling the vendor at the number
  already on file. Never act on banking details sent by email.
- Gift cards: not purchased with the P-card except for the annual staff recognition program run by HR.
- P-card statements are reconciled monthly; the office manager receives a quarterly summary.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# RM-100 Records retention (excerpt)

| Record | Keep |
| --- | --- |
| Project files (drawings, calculations, correspondence, as-builts) | 10 years after substantial completion (Ohio's statute of repose, ORC 2305.131) |
| Accounting records, invoices | 7 years after the fiscal year |
| Expense reports | 7 years |
| Visitor logs | 2 years |
| Meeting minutes | permanent |

A legal hold from the General Counsel suspends all destruction of the records it names, paper and electronic,
until Legal releases it in writing. Destruction lists are approved by the office manager.
Requests for project records from outside the firm (other than the client under contract) go to Legal.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Employee handbook (excerpts)

- Compensation and personnel information is shared only with people HR names. Employment and salary
  verifications go to HR (hrverify@corwinleffel.com or 317-555-0120); staff do not confirm employment or pay.
- Visitors sign in with Envoy at the front desk and wear a badge; the host meets them.
- Meeting minutes record decisions and actions, not discussion. The chair reviews minutes before they are
  distributed. Closed sessions (personnel, compensation) are not minuted. Minutes stay inside the firm unless the
  chair says otherwise.

versions.content:
# FIN-150 Timekeeping (rev. 2025-01-01)

1. Timesheets are weekly, Monday to Sunday, and due in Vantagepoint by 10:00 the following Monday.
2. Payroll locks the period at 12:00 Tuesday. Hours entered after the lock are paid with the next payroll as a
   correction.
3. Each employee enters and signs their own timesheet, including when traveling or in the field (Vantagepoint
   works in a phone browser). Nobody enters, changes or signs time for another employee. Group administrators
   send reminders; they do not enter time.
4. Project managers approve their projects' hours by 10:00 Tuesday.
5. The group administrator tells the group manager of any timesheet still missing at the lock.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ADM-310 Mail, deliveries and checks received (regional offices)

- The front desk opens and logs incoming mail each morning, except envelopes marked Personal, Confidential,
  HR or Legal, which go to the addressee unopened.
- Project mail is scanned to the addressee and the project file the same day; the original goes to the
  addressee's tray.
- Checks received: record payer, check number, date, amount and invoice in the mail log; scan a copy to the
  project file; send the original to HQ Accounts Receivable by FedEx Priority Overnight the same day and email
  AR the details and the tracking number. Checks are never held in the office or handed to project staff.
- Certified mail and return receipts (green cards) are logged and filed with the project.
- Packages are logged in Envoy Deliveries; the recipient is notified automatically.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# ADM-330 Notary services (Columbus)

The Columbus office has two commissioned Ohio notaries public for firm business: Renee Castell and Carol
Mendes. Ohio notarial acts follow ORC Chapter 147.

- The signer appears in person before the notary, shows current government photo ID, and signs in the
  notary's presence (a jurat) or acknowledges their signature to the notary in person (an acknowledgment).
- Never notarize a document signed outside your presence by someone who does not appear before you, a blank or
  incomplete document, or your own or a relative's document.
- Record every notarial act in the office notary log: date, signer, document, type of act, ID seen.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# FIN-121 P-card cardholder rules (excerpt)

- The card number, expiry date and security code are never sent by email, chat or text, and never given to a
  caller. Pay on the merchant's own website or by calling the merchant at a number you looked up yourself.
- Keep an itemized receipt for every charge. Reconcile the monthly statement within 10 days of the cycle close:
  code each charge, attach receipts, and dispute errors (duplicates, wrong amounts) with the merchant first and
  then the card issuer.
- Sales tax is paid; Corwin Leffel is not tax-exempt.

# Columbus office info

- Hours 8:00-5:00. Front desk 614-555-0100. Suite 400, 175 S Third St.
